name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '18' is the dispatch-table index (idx 0x18 of the per-event handler table at 0x51B91; entry at 0x51BF1 holds this function's address), a meaningful domain ID, not address residue. Descriptor corrected from '__unref_dialog' to '__ch7_captain_defeat': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch7 kill-drop path -- ch7 char_spawn_record[24] = the royal guard captain (elite 突擊騎兵, enemy_data 15, char_id 0x53, lv12) carries pickup_kind=2 param=0x18, so the captain's death dispatches consequence[0x18]. The body shows the captain's dying line (page 3). The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path.
purpose: Chapter 7 royal-guard-captain defeat dialog (dispatch slot idx 0x18, reached via the ch7 kill-drop path): when the captain (record[24] elite 突擊騎兵, pickup_kind=2 param=0x18) falls, it shows chapter-text dialog page 3 (char 0x21, the dying captain, realizing the party was framed) and returns.
logic_summary: Straight-line, no-branch. After the compiler-injected __CHK(0x28) stack probe, it calls fd2_display_dialog_scene(data_fd2_current_chapter_text, page=3, 0xA0000, 0x140, 0xCD, 0x4C, 0x4A, 0x13, 1) and returns. No portrait reload, no camera pan, no global state writes, no RNG; the dialog call's return value is discarded. In the original binary the body is PUSH 0x28; CALL __CHK, then falls through into the 8-PUSH chain at 0x34906 which JMPs (0x3491F -> 0x34C0F) into the shared tail of fd2_show_chapter_dialog_with_portrait_set_1. It also exposes a Class-3 shared entry at 0x34901 (the CALL __CHK instruction) that fd2_chapter_event_handler_22 @ 0x34C6C borrows via PUSH 0x28; JMP 0x34901, reusing this entire body. Reproduced as a single inline dialog call for Layer-2 equivalence.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: The uniform per-event dispatch argument from the handler table at 0x51B91 (1-arg cdecl; the kill-drop recipient/killer idx). The body never reads it.
params.reason: Descriptive of the uniform dispatch-table arg, no address residue. The body does not consume it; matches the convention used across sibling handlers in chevt1.c.

returns.semantics: No return value (void). fd2_display_dialog_scene's uint32 return is discarded.
